title: DeepSeek-R1
summary: Gets reasoning out of reinforcement learning against verifiable answers, with little or no supervised reasoning data first.

title: DeepSeek-V3
summary: A mixture-of-experts model trained for a fraction of the usual cost, with the parallelism and FP8 detail most reports omit.

title: Actions Speak Louder than Words
summary: Recasts recommendation as sequential transduction, so one large sequence model replaces a feature-engineering stack.

title: vLLM
summary: Manages the KV cache in fixed-size pages like virtual memory, since fragmentation was what limited serving throughput.

title: Direct Preference Optimization
summary: Shows the RLHF objective has a closed form optimizable on preference pairs, removing the reward model and the RL loop.

title: LLaMA
summary: Trains smaller models on far more tokens than compute-optimal, because inference cost is what a deployed model charges you.

title: Whisper
summary: Trains on a very large weakly-labelled multilingual set, and gets robustness without per-dataset fine-tuning.

title: DynamoDB
summary: Fifteen years of running a managed key-value service, and what predictable performance actually costs to deliver.

title: Redshift Re-invented
summary: What a decade of customer workloads changed in the warehouse: automatic tuning, and compute separated from managed storage.

title: FlashAttention
summary: Computes exact attention without ever materializing the attention matrix, by tiling the work to fit in SRAM.

title: InstructGPT
summary: Fine-tunes on human demonstrations, then optimizes against a reward model learned from preference comparisons.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
summary: Showing the model worked examples with intermediate steps makes it produce reasoning steps, and answers improve.

title: LoRA
summary: Freezes the pretrained weights and trains a low-rank update, which makes a fine-tune small and swappable.

title: Switch Transformers
summary: Routes each token to a single expert instead of a dense layer, so parameter count grows without proportional compute.

title: TiDB
summary: Serves analytics off a columnar replica kept over Raft, so one system does OLTP and OLAP without a separate pipeline.

title: CockroachDB
summary: Serializable geo-distributed transactions without special clocks, using hybrid logical clocks and reads that refresh their timestamp.

title: GPT-3
summary: Shows scale alone gets a language model to do tasks from examples in the prompt, with no gradient updates.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
summary: Finds loss follows smooth power laws in parameters, data and compute, which turned model sizing into extrapolation.

title: DLRM
summary: An open reference architecture for recommendation, and the parallelism its embedding tables force on you.

title: Presto
summary: A distributed SQL engine that queries data where it lives across many connectors rather than requiring a load.

title: BERT
summary: Pre-trains a bidirectional transformer with masked language modelling, then fine-tunes it per task.

title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Drops recurrence and convolution for self-attention, making sequence modelling parallel over positions.

title: Aurora
summary: Pushes redo log application into the storage layer, because the network, not the disk, was the bottleneck.

title: BBR
summary: Models the bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip time instead of treating loss as the congestion signal.

title: YouTube Recommendations
summary: Splits recommendation into candidate generation and ranking, and trains on watch time rather than clicks.

title: Snowflake
summary: Separates storage from compute so each scales and is billed on its own, over shared object storage.

title: Borg
summary: Mixes services and batch jobs on the same machines, overcommitting to batch and reclaiming when services need it.

title: f4
summary: Moves BLOBs that have stopped being read from full replication to erasure coding, splitting the tier by access pattern.

title: Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
summary: Decision-tree features feeding a linear online learner, and the finding that data freshness mattered more than the model class.

title: Raft
summary: A consensus algorithm built for understandability, keeping leader election, log replication and safety separate.

title: B4
summary: Google's software-defined WAN, run near full utilization by treating inter-datacenter bandwidth as a global optimization.

title: TAO
summary: A read-optimized store for the social graph that replaces per-object cache logic with an objects-and-associations API.

title: word2vec
summary: Trains word vectors with a shallow model cheap enough for a billion words, and finds analogies as vector arithmetic.

title: Spanner
summary: Global transactions with external consistency, by waiting out the bounded clock uncertainty TrueTime reports.

title: Kafka
summary: A distributed log rather than a queue: messages persist, consumers track their own offsets, writes stay sequential.

title: ZooKeeper
summary: A coordination service with a wait-free, filesystem-like API, so applications build locks instead of embedding consensus.

title: The Origin of Quorum Systems
summary: Traces quorum systems from plain majorities through Byzantine and probabilistic variants, and what each trades away.

title: HDFS
summary: The open reimplementation of GFS, written up with the operational consequences of its single namenode.

title: Dapper
summary: Distributed tracing by propagating a trace id through RPCs, on the finding that aggressive sampling still finds latency.

title: Cassandra
summary: Dynamo's ring and replication with Bigtable's column-family data model, built for Facebook's inbox search.

title: Dynamo
summary: Chooses availability over consistency: consistent hashing, tunable quorums, and version conflicts the application resolves.

title: Paxos Made Live
summary: What it took to turn Paxos into Chubby's replicated log, where the algorithm was the small part.

title: Bigtable
summary: A sparse, sorted, distributed map over GFS, rows split into tablets, with no cross-row transactions.

title: Chubby
summary: A coarse-grained lock service that gives the rest of Google leader election, so other systems need not implement Paxos.

title: Ceph
summary: Takes the metadata server out of the data path by having clients compute placement with CRUSH.

title: Gossip Based Membership
summary: Proves the overlay a gossip membership protocol maintains stays connected for a time exponential in the square of the view size.

title: MapReduce
summary: Reduces distributed batch computation to two user functions, leaving partitioning, scheduling and retries to the framework.

title: The Google File System
summary: Assumes hardware fails constantly and files are huge and append-mostly: one metadata master, replicated 64MB chunks.

title: Paxos Made Simple
summary: Lamport's re-explanation of Paxos: majority quorums reach agreement with no synchronized clocks.

title: Sagas
summary: Splits a long-lived transaction into steps that commit as they go, each paired with a compensating transaction that undoes it.

title: Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events
summary: Defines happened-before as a partial order over events, and shows a logical clock can respect it without synchronized time.
